3	
4	  Blueprint chapter: blueprint/src/chapters/IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_1_C_1.tex
5	  Source report:     reports/ipho_2026_k3/problem_IPhO_2026_1_C_1.source.json
6	  Official page:     T1_page-3.png  (IPhO 2026 Theoretical Exam, page 6/14)
7	
8	  Physical situation (Figure 1c):
9	  A photon of angular frequency `ω` strikes an ozone molecule `O₃` at rest and
10	  is absorbed, dissociating it into an oxygen molecule `O₂` and an oxygen atom
11	  `O`.  The ground-state energies of `O₃` and of the fragments are `Uᵢ` and
12	  `U_f`, with `ΔU = U_f - Uᵢ > 0`.  The momentum of the outgoing `O₂` makes
13	  the angle `θ` with the incident photon direction.  The fragments are treated
14	  classically and non-relativistically; an oxygen atom has mass `m`, so the
15	  `O₂` fragment has mass `2m`; the photon momentum is `p_γ = E_γ/c = ℏω/c`.
16	
17	  Current subquestion (T1-C1, 2.5 pts):
18	    Determine the minimum angular frequency `ω_min` required for the
19	    dissociation to occur at outgoing `O₂` angle `θ`, in terms of
20	    `ℏ, c, θ, ΔU` and `m`.
21	
22	  Recorded official answer:
23	    for `θ ≤ π/2`,
24	      `ω_min = 3 m c² (1 - √(1 - (2 ΔU / (3 m c²)) (2 sin²θ + 1))) /
25	                 (ℏ (2 sin²θ + 1))`;
26	    for `θ ≥ π/2`, the same threshold evaluated at `θ = π/2`.
27	  (Official solution, `T1_solution.txt`: the threshold is the smallest root of
28	  `(cos 2θ - 2) ℏ²ω² + 6 m c² ℏω - 6 ΔU m c² = 0`, and
29	  `2 sin²θ + 1 = 2 - cos 2θ`.)
30	
31	  All theorem statements below are faithful contracts.  The current target
32	  conclusion — the closed-form value of `ω_min` — appears only on the
33	  conclusion side of the main theorems `minimum_angular_frequency_T1_C1` /
34	  `minimum_angular_frequency_backward_branch_T1_C1` and of the auxiliary
35	  quadratic-form lemma `quadratic_characterization_of_threshold`; the
36	  governing-law predicates (`IsTwoBodyDissociation`, `IsScatteringAngle`)
37	  never mention it.
38	
39	  Iter-017 redraft (proof-Review certificate `needs_redraft`,
40	  other_modeling_defect): the official solution attains the threshold at the
41	  degenerate critical configuration `p = 0` (the `O₂` fragment at rest, the
42	  `O` atom carrying the full photon momentum) for every `θ ≥ π/2`, including
43	  the forward theorem's boundary `θ = π/2` — the tangent point of the
44	  velocity circle at `θ = 90°` is the origin, and for larger angles the
45	  threshold circle passes through the origin (`T1_solution.txt`, T1-C1).
46	  Accordingly `IsScatteringAngle` no longer excludes `p = 0`, and the
47	  backward theorem's discriminant hypothesis is the real-square-root
48	  condition at `π/2`, `0 ≤ 1 − 2ΔU/(mc²)`; the earlier
49	  `0 ≤ 1 − 2ΔU/(3mc²)` admitted the regime `ΔU ∈ (mc²/2, 3mc²/2]`, where
50	  nothing at all is reachable at backward angles.  The two reachability
51	  conjuncts remain `sorry` (proof-lane work); every other proof in the file —
52	  in particular both minimality conjuncts — is unchanged and never used the
53	  dropped `p ≠ 0`.

56	import Mathlib
57	
58	open Real Set
59	
60	noncomputable section
61	
62	namespace IPhO2026.Problem1.C1
63	
64	section UniversalConstants
65	
66	/-!
67	Universal constants and molecular data of the problem.  They are declared as
68	abstract scalars (with their SI roles recorded in the docstrings) rather than
69	transparent aliases, so that the contracts below cannot be closed by
70	unfolding.
71	-/
72	
73	/-- Reduced Planck constant `ℏ` (J·s). -/
74	opaque hbar : ℝ
75	
76	/-- Speed of light in vacuum `c` (m/s). -/
77	opaque speedOfLight : ℝ
78	
79	/-- Mass `m` of one oxygen atom (kg); the `O₂` fragment has mass `2m`. -/
80	opaque oxygenAtomMass : ℝ
81	
82	/-- Photon angular frequency `ω` for any photon considered in this process
83	    (rad/s).  The closed-form value of `ω_min` is a *target*, not a datum. -/
84	opaque photonAngularFrequency : ℝ
85	
86	/-- Ground-state energy `Uᵢ` of the ozone molecule `O₃` (J). -/
87	opaque ozoneGroundStateEnergy : ℝ
88	
89	/-- Ground-state energy `U_f` of the photofragments `O₂ + O` (J). -/
90	opaque fragmentsGroundStateEnergy : ℝ
91	
92	/-- Energy gap `ΔU = U_f − Uᵢ` (J): the energy that must be supplied to
93	    dissociate ozone at rest into `O₂ + O`. -/
94	def dissociationEnergyGap : ℝ :=
95	  fragmentsGroundStateEnergy - ozoneGroundStateEnergy
96	
97	/-- Positivity of the universal constants (physical regime of the problem). -/
98	structure ConstantRegime : Prop where
99	  hbar_pos : 0 < hbar
100	  speedOfLight_pos : 0 < speedOfLight
101	  oxygenAtomMass_pos : 0 < oxygenAtomMass
102	  /-- The dissociation is endothermic: `ΔU > 0`. -/
103	  gap_pos : 0 < dissociationEnergyGap
104	
105	end UniversalConstants
106	
107	section ReactionGeometry
108	
109	/-!
110	Geometry of the reaction (Figure 1c).  The incoming photon and the two
111	outgoing fragments are coplanar; the `O₂` momentum `p⃗` makes the angle `θ`
112	with the incident photon direction.  Vectors live in an abstract Euclidean
113	2-space so that the momentum-conservation law is a genuine vector equation.
114	-/
115	
116	/-- The plane containing the incident photon and the outgoing fragments in
117	    Figure 1c: a two-dimensional Euclidean space.  Using an abstract inner
118	    product space (rather than coordinate pairs of reals) keeps the notion of
119	    *angle between momentum vectors* intrinsic. -/
120	abbrev ReactionPlane : Type := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)
121	
122	/-- The direction of the incident photon (and of its momentum) in the
123	    reaction plane: a unit vector. -/
124	structure PhotonLine where
125	  direction : ReactionPlane
126	  direction_unit : ‖direction‖ = 1
127	
128	/-- `θ` is the angle between the outgoing `O₂` momentum `p` and the incident
129	    photon direction `k̂`, as read from Figure 1c: the cosine-law component
130	    statement `⟪k̂, p⟫ = ‖p‖ * cos θ`.
131	
132	    For `p ≠ 0` this is exactly the statement that `θ` is the angle between
133	    the two momentum vectors.  The degenerate case `p = 0` — the `O₂`
134	    fragment produced at rest, with the `O` atom carrying the full photon
135	    momentum — is admitted: the cosine law is then vacuous (`0 = 0`) at every
136	    `θ`.  This matches the official solution (`T1_solution.txt`, T1-C1): the
137	    tangent critical configuration at `θ = 90°` is the origin point of the
138	    velocity circle, and for `θ ≥ 90°` the threshold circle passes through
139	    the origin, so the official answer counts the threshold as *attained* at
140	    `p = 0`.  Excluding `p = 0` would make the threshold an unattained
141	    infimum and both main theorems below false (proof-Review certificate,
142	    iter-017). -/
143	def IsScatteringAngle (k : PhotonLine) (p : ReactionPlane) (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
144	  @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction p = ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ
145	
146	/-- The angular range of the problem: `θ ∈ [0, π]`.  The branch information
147	    (`θ ≤ π/2` versus `θ ≥ π/2`) is preserved by hypothesis, not selected
148	    only in the conclusion. -/
149	def IsAngularRange (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
150	  θ ∈ Icc 0 Real.pi
151	
152	/-- The forward / non-backscattering branch of the official solution:
153	    `θ ≤ π/2`.  The official solution warns that the tangent-line critical
154	    configuration of Figure 1c exists only in this branch; for `θ ≥ π/2` the
155	    threshold freezes at its `θ = π/2` value. -/
156	def IsForwardBranch (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
157	  θ ≤ Real.pi / 2
158	
159	end ReactionGeometry
160	
161	section GoverningLaws
162	
163	/-!
164	Governing physical laws.  These predicates state the modelling relations
165	directly (photon momentum `p_γ = ℏω/c`, vector momentum conservation with
166	the Figure-1c angle readout, and non-relativistic energy balance with
167	fragment masses `2m` and `m`).  None of them mentions the closed-form
168	threshold that the current subquestion asks to determine.
169	-/
170	
171	/-- Lawful configurations of the absorption + two-body breakup
172	    `γ + O₃ → O₂ + O` in Figure 1c.  Every field is a constraining equation
173	    that a later proof can rewrite with:
174	
175	    * `momentum_q_sq` — vector momentum conservation `ℏω/c · k̂ = p⃗ + q⃗`,
176	      eliminated to the cosine-law component statement
177	      `‖q‖² = (ℏω/c)² + ‖p‖² − 2 (ℏω/c) ‖p‖ cos θ`;
178	    * `q_unique` — the vector equation determines `q` uniquely as
179	      `q = (ℏω/c) • k̂ − p`;
180	    * `angle_readout` — the Figure-1c readout that `θ` is the angle between
181	      `p⃗` and the incident photon direction;
182	    * `energy_balance` — non-relativistic energy conservation
183	      `ℏω = ΔU + ‖p‖²/(2·2m) + ‖q‖²/(2m)`.
184	
185	    None of the fields quantifies over configurations or mentions the
186	    minimum; those appear only on the conclusion side of the theorems below. -/
187	structure IsTwoBodyDissociation
188	    (k : PhotonLine) (ω θ m dU : ℝ) (p q : ReactionPlane) : Prop where
189	  /-- Cosine-law magnitude equation from `ℏω/c · k̂ = p⃗ + q⃗`:
190	      `‖q‖² = (ℏω/c)² + ‖p‖² − 2 (ℏω/c) ‖p‖ cos θ`. -/
191	  momentum_q_sq :
192	    ‖q‖ ^ 2 = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) ^ 2 + ‖p‖ ^ 2
193	      - 2 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ
194	  /-- The vector momentum balance determines the `O` momentum uniquely as
195	      `q = (ℏω/c) • k̂ − p`. -/
196	  q_unique : q = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) • k.direction - p
197	  /-- Figure-1c angle readout between the photon direction and `p`. -/
198	  angle_readout : IsScatteringAngle k p θ
199	  /-- Non-relativistic energy balance: the photon energy `ℏω` covers the
200	      dissociation gap `ΔU` plus the classical kinetic energies of the `O₂`
201	      fragment (mass `2m`) and the `O` fragment (mass `m`). -/
202	  energy_balance :
203	    hbar * ω = dU + ‖p‖ ^ 2 / (2 * (2 * m)) + ‖q‖ ^ 2 / (2 * m)
204

206	    consequence of the vector momentum balance and the angle readout, so the
207	    `momentum_q_sq` field is the eliminated shadow of `q_unique` rather than
208	    an independent modelling assumption.  Recording this implication is what
209	    makes the interface constraining: any countermodel must satisfy a vector
210	    equation, not just an isolated scalar identity. -/

214	    (hθ : IsScatteringAngle k p θ) :

216	      - 2 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := by
217	  have hinner : @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction p = ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := hθ
218	  set a : ℝ := hbar * ω / speedOfLight with ha
219	  have hk : @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction k.direction = 1 := by
220	    rw [@inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, k.direction_unit]
221	    norm_num
222	  have hsq : ‖q‖ ^ 2 = @inner ℝ _ _ q q := by
223	    rw [@inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K]
224	    norm_num
225	  calc ‖q‖ ^ 2 = @inner ℝ _ _ q q := hsq
